A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, equations, figures and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably despite added examples, renumbering and layout adjustments.

before.justification: v1 reports original analyses of 1,000 Reddit texts and 300 generated stegotexts, token-rank distributions, cross-model scoring, and model-quality and runtime comparisons.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds generated-output comparisons for rank inversion and an alternate-key deniability example in Figures 9 and 15.

M1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds an optional reversal of the rank sequence before stegotext generation to improve steering. This extends the procedure, while the basic rank-based encoder/decoder, optional prompts and two-model vocabulary adaptation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Figure 15 extends demonstrated task coverage to alternate-key deniability using toy board-game messages. v1 discussed deniability but did not report this recovery example. Existing Reddit, code, chess, dialect and other text coverage is retained.

E2.justification: New Figure 9 explicitly compares the rank-inversion variant against the original, unreversed procedure for the same message and prompt. Existing random-string controls and the six-model comparison are retained; no cited steganography algorithm is newly benchmarked.

E3.justification: The added demonstrations introduce a same-message/same-prompt rank-order comparison and genuine-versus-bogus-key decoding with a shared game-specific prefix. The existing 1,000-text corpus, 85-token truncation, three sets of 100 stegotexts and log-probability evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 9 adds a qualitative ablation testing whether rank reversal reduces steering failure. Figure 15 adds a worked deniability case. Existing domain, model-quality, initial-token-rank and cross-model plausibility analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Run/seed disclosures and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. The retained rank-position plot uses the same medians, 25th–75th percentile boxes and 20th–80th percentile whiskers. The new examples introduce no repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Retained quantitative plots and model runtimes are unchanged. Figure 9 adds an example labelled as better steering with reversed ranks. Figure 15 newly reports log probabilities of -132 for the stegotext, -107 for the true message and -115 for the bogus-key message.

T1.justification: The probability definition, brute-force bound and Appendix A.4 vocabulary-mapping reasoning are retained. The new footnote supplies the standard perplexity formula and an explanatory caveat; it introduces no new formal result, proof or assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about equal-token-length hiding, steerability, small-model efficiency and implications for intentionality and AI safety. Naming the protocol Calgacus and adding supporting examples do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 explains rank inversion through the stabilizing effect of established context before high-rank choices. A new footnote explains why perplexity normalization may retain length bias. The deniability discussion gains a concrete illustration, while existing applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: The new examples disclose the inversion input, secret prompt and rank sequence, plus the deniability example's genuine/bogus keys and shared message prefix. Existing quantization, hardware, llama.cpp, runtime and companion-code access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Ziegler et al. (2019) as early neural linguistic steganography and replaces Brown et al. (2020) with the already-cited Radford et al. (2019) for LLM background. Positioning relative to Meteor, Wu et al. and Zamir remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Limited edits introduce Calgacus throughout, explain its name, expand the prompting discussion and add the perplexity footnote. Section ordering and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 9 and 15 add rank-inversion and deniability displays. The retained rank-position and Phi-3 plots become Figures 10 and 14 and share pages with the additions. Existing plot content is unchanged, with localized layout and cross-reference adjustments.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.5 and Figure 9 add a practical response to the previously documented steering failure, while Figure 15 makes the deniability argument inspectable through explicit keys and outputs. These improve usefulness and evidential clarity modestly. Their single-example scope leaves general robustness and security unresolved, and the main quantitative evaluation is unchanged.
